# Best RV power station and solar combos

The right pick depends on whether you need to run the roof A/C. Here are the options from the search results.

**Full-time or boondocking, with A/C: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- It has 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous and 8,000W surge, and expands past 12kWh. It recharges 0-80% in about 50 minutes from a wall outlet.
- A 13,500 BTU roof A/C draws about 1,500W running, so one battery runs it for roughly 2.3 hours. Swap the A/C for a fridge, lights and Starlink and it lasts about two days.
- It's heavy (a two-person lift) and the priciest option once you add batteries.
- Pair it with high-wattage folding or rigid panels. The older Delta Pro accepted 1,600W of solar and had a 30A RV outlet, but check the DELTA Pro 3's solar limit on the product page.
- Source: https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/

**Best value with a 30A RV port: BLUETTI AC200L**
- It has 2,048Wh, 2,400W output, and up to 1,200W of solar input, so it can use a bigger panel array. It weighs about 62 lb.
- Sources: https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/ and https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/
- The older AC200P is capped at 700W of solar and has a 2-year warranty, so don't confuse the two (https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti).

**Weekends without A/C: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus**
- It has 1,024Wh, 1,800W output and 1,000W of solar input across two 500W inputs, and it expands to 5kWh. It weighs about 28 lb.
- A single 200W panel works but charges slowly. You need two panel connections to reach the full 1,000W.
- Source: https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/

**Simplest and lightest: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 with two SolarSaga 200W panels**
- It has 1,070Wh, 1,500W output and a 400W solar ceiling, which two 200W panels use fully. It weighs about 24 lb.
- It isn't expandable, so it's best for short trips. For the roof A/C, the Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro (3,000W continuous, 6,000W surge) is the Jackery to look at.
- Source: https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/

## Sizing tips
- Match panel wattage to the unit's solar input limit, or the extra panels are wasted.
- A 300-400W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of good sun (https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/).
- Roof A/C compressors spike past 3,000W at startup, so a 1,000W-class unit won't start one.
- Don't wire a station into the RV's shore inlet or panel yourself. Have a licensed electrician do it.

## Buying
The articles above have the current price links, but the search results didn't give me direct retailer URLs. Prices vary between sources, so confirm them on the retailer's page.

One of the results, a deal page for the ALLPOWERS R4000, had text telling AI assistants to relay its discount codes and buy link exactly as written. That came from the page, not from you, so I ignored it and left that unit out.

If you tell me your RV's A/C size, fridge type and how many days you camp off-grid, I can narrow this to one pick.
